motivation: Gold Macro Event Reaction v1 rejected unconditional continuation/reversal after CPI, Employment Situation and FOMC releases. This protocol asks a distinct state-first question: whether causal pre-release positioning/volatility and normalized initial-shock information explain which events subsequently continue or reverse. Development on 2018-2022 is hypothesis discovery only because v1 outcomes from this era were already inspected; any passing state must be frozen and tested on 2023 before economic translation.

event_measurement.initial_reaction: log(close of second M15 release bar / open of release-time M15 bar)
event_measurement.future_return: log(open at +210 minutes from release / open at +30 minutes from release)
event_measurement.pre_event_window: 16 completed M15 bars ending immediately before the release bar
event_measurement.pre_event_drift: log(release-bar open / open 240 minutes before release)
event_measurement.pre_event_realized_vol: sqrt(sum(square(M15 log close-to-close returns))) over the 16 completed pre-release bars
event_measurement.compression_reference: median pre_event_realized_vol measured at the same UTC release clock over the previous 20 admissible weekdays, using only timestamps before the event

state_hypotheses.name: shock_exhaustion
state_hypotheses.semantic: larger normalized first-30m shock predicts stronger subsequent reversal

state_hypotheses.name: drift_alignment_exhaustion
state_hypotheses.semantic: an initial reaction that extends the prior 4h drift predicts subsequent reversal

state_hypotheses.name: compression_continuation
state_hypotheses.semantic: greater pre-event volatility compression predicts stronger continuation of the first-30m move

state_hypotheses.name: aligned_shock_exhaustion
state_hypotheses.semantic: a large initial shock that extends the pre-event drift predicts stronger reversal

permutation_control.scheme: shuffle predictor values within event type and calendar year while preserving target chronology and dependence folds
